tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...', 'Load it yourself before delegating'), focuses on user intent (auditing who can invoke Bedrock, triaging GuardDuty findings, phasing out keys) rather than implementation details, and explicitly lists many trigger contexts (dormant/old/root keys, SCP impact, GuardDuty findings) as well as explicit out-of-scope cases (cost, failing calls). It is dense but remains within a reasonable paragraph length for a complex skill.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when someone asks this, wants to list or phase out long-term Amazon Bedrock API keys, asks about dormant, old or root keys with Amazon Bedrock access, triages a GuardDuty AI Protection finding such as Impact:IAMUser/AnomalousModelInvocation..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but nearly every sentence conveys project-specific facts: AWS API quirks, masking rules, catalog check-ids, LLM-BPA tiers, and tool limitations (e.g. AWS DevOps Agent's tool not running the policy simulator). It does not explain general concepts like what IAM or Bedrock is.
tests.evidence: AWS DevOps Agent's AWS tool does not run the IAM policy simulator.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body consistently delegates detailed material (catalogs, tier rules, API quirks, snapshot mechanics) to references/ files rather than inlining it, even within conditional Router rows which just name which reference to load.
tests.evidence: The rules are in `references/checks-credentials.md`. ... Apply the catalog exactly: never invent a tier, a reason or a threshold.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ is linked via markdown link syntax somewhere in the body (e.g., policy-evaluation.md, checks-credentials.md, collection-reference.md, policy-snapshot.md, evaluation-outcomes.md, api-quirks.md, remediation-guidance.md, out-of-scope-routing.md, metrics-and-logs.md).
tests.evidence: `references/out-of-scope-routing.md` gives each case in full: load it when a request is not only an audit of long-lived credentials.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: References specify when to load each file, e.g. loading out-of-scope-routing.md 'when a request is not only an audit' or loading policy-snapshot/evaluation/outcomes before specific IAM calls.
tests.evidence: Before any `iam:GetAccountAuthorizationDetails`, `iam:GetPolicy`, `iam:GetPolicyVersion` or `iam:GetContextKeysForPrincipalPolicy` call, load this skill and read `references/policy-snapshot.md`, `references/policy-evaluation.md` and `references/evaluation-outcomes.md`.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (masking rules, policy evaluation order, tier scoring) are given exact prescriptive steps, while answer-format flexibility ('Answer the question asked, in any format') is explicitly left open for the agent when appropriate.
tests.evidence: Answer the question asked, in any format, and keep every must-keep item.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The Router table gives a clear default call/sequence per scenario rather than presenting equal alternative options; where multiple remediation templates exist, each is tied to a specific scenario rather than offered as interchangeable choices.
tests.evidence: | Phase out or forbid long-term Amazon Bedrock API keys, keeping short-term ones | The API key inventory, then the users whose allowed actions include `iam:CreateServiceSpecificCredential` | `references/remediation-guidance.md` (section 3.3), `assets/remediation/policy-deny-long-term-bedrock-api-keys.json` |

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure and Router teach a generalizable approach (scope the accounts, inventory credentials, evaluate policies, score tiers, present) applicable across varied audit requests, not a one-off declaration for a single instance.
tests.evidence: Work through one account at a time, taking the steps below in their numbered order and ticking each one off as it is done.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The 'Common wrong answers' section functions as a gotchas section, documenting concrete, non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain (e.g., last-use semantics, Info tier meaning, API key quirks).
tests.evidence: "The key was used yesterday, so it is calling Amazon Bedrock." Last use is the key's last call to any AWS service. It shows the key is in use, not what it called.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured audit reports and provides a dedicated template asset for this purpose.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body does not inline the report template; it only describes the structure at a high level (Scope, Findings columns, Summary) and defers the actual template to assets/.
tests.evidence: the report follows after a line `---`... the Findings columns TIER to CHECKS.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All assets files are referenced: bedrock-permissions-report-template.md, delegation-prompt.md, and each file under assets/remediation/ (scp-deny-bedrock-to-iam-users.json, scp-restrict-bedrock-regions-models.json, policy-deny-bedrock-api-keys.json, policy-deny-long-term-bedrock-api-keys.json) are all named in the Appendix and/or Router.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Asset links specify when to use them, tied to specific scenarios in the Router table and Delegating section.
tests.evidence: **Delegating** is allowed, with `assets/delegation-prompt.md`. The agent that delegates may not have read this skill, so a sub-agent that runs this audit starts its reply with the answer...

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: All asset references use relative paths like assets/bedrock-permissions-report-template.md and assets/remediation/*.json with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labeling as required, satisfying the format requirement for procedural workflows.
tests.evidence: - [ ] Step 1: Fix the scope and parameters... - [ ] Step 2: Name each account with `iam:ListAccountAliases`...

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Before You Present' checklist instructing the agent to validate its own draft output (tiers, masking, completeness) before presenting to the user, which is self-validation rather than procedural work.
tests.evidence: Check every item with your draft in hand, and answer only when each one holds. ... Every row's tier came from the tier rules applied in order...
